summary: Dispatch independent native Metal scene kernels from device-written live contact and per-color counts while retaining compiled capacity strides.
regressions: Native Metal tracked/untracked indirect dispatch test covers zero and changing counts and nonzero byte offsets; descriptor validators reject missing and out-of-range buffers.
Focused scene execution tests cover overflowing producer inputs, empty and multiple-batch color ranges, and fresh Rust colored-solver output.
differences: Only Metal runtime scene specialization opts in; other backends retain static launch plans. Cooperative radix and scan launches are unchanged.

Producer grids are trusted kernel outputs, bounded by compiled capacity; no solver data is read to CPU to choose grids. Full parity evidence remains stale; existing production-reference divergence and missing Ascend/CUDA qualification remain open.
